title: A wish to speak to all
summary: Alma wishes he could speak to every people and declare repentance and the plan of redemption to every soul.

explicit_facts.text: Alma wishes he were an angel and could cry repentance unto every people.
Alma wishes to declare repentance and the plan of redemption to every soul, so that people would repent and sorrow would cease across the earth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma's wish can be presented without depicting it as an event.
unspecified_visual_details: Alma's appearance and location are not specified.
No angel, trumpet, or worldwide audience is described as physically present.

spoken_dialogue.text: O that I were an angel, and could have the wish of mine heart,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma

spoken_dialogue.text: Yea, I would declare unto every soul, as with the voice of thunder, repentance and the plan of redemption,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The angel, thunderous voice, and worldwide proclamation are part of Alma's wish, not narrated events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Alma becoming an angel or actually addressing every people.
Do not depict a literal trumpet, earth-shaking voice, or sorrow-free world.

title: Content with his calling
summary: The speaker reflects that he is a man and should be content with what the Lord allotted him, rather than desire more than God's decrees.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says he is a man and ought to be content with what the Lord allotted him.
He says God grants and allots according to people's desires and wills, toward life or death, salvation or destruction.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Off-screen reflective narration can continue over an unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker's appearance, location, and any surrounding objects are unspecified.

narration.text: I ought to be content with the things which the Lord hath allotted unto me.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The statements about decrees and allotment are teachings, not visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not literalize God's decrees as visible actions or objects.

title: Desire and choice
summary: The speaker reflects that good and evil are before people, and asks why he should desire more than to do the work to which he was called.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says good and evil have come before all people; those who know neither are blameless, while those who know them receive according to their desires.
He asks why he should desire more than to perform the work to which he was called.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Present this as off-screen reflection rather than illustrating abstract outcomes.
unspecified_visual_details: No people choosing between good and evil, or setting, is specified.

narration.text: good and evil have come before all men
why should I desire more than to perform the work to which I have been called?

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The alternatives of life, death, joy, and remorse are part of the teaching, not separate visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage symbolic or supernatural depictions of salvation, destruction, or conscience.

title: The Lord teaches among nations
summary: The speaker questions his wish to speak to the whole earth and reflects that the Lord grants nations teachers of their own nation and tongue, according to wisdom.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker asks why he should wish to be an angel who could speak to all the earth.
He says the Lord grants all nations teachers of their own nation and tongue, giving what is fitting in wisdom.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use off-screen narration over a neutral setting; no teacher or nation is individually depicted by the verses.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker, teachers, nations, and setting have no specified appearance.

narration.text: Why should I desire that I were an angel
the Lord doth counsel in wisdom, according to that which is just and true.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The wish to speak everywhere remains hypothetical.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the speaker as an angel or invent specific teachers, languages, or audiences.

title: Joy in the work
summary: The speaker glories in the Lord's command and in the possibility of bringing souls to repentance; he describes joy when he sees brethren repent and remembers the Lord's mercy to him.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says he glories in what the Lord commanded and hopes to be an instrument in bringing a soul to repentance.
He says he feels joy when he sees many brethren repent and come to the Lord, and remembers that the Lord heard his prayer and extended mercy to him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Off-screen narration can carry the speaker's reflection; the remembered prayer and mercy are not depicted as separate present action.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker's appearance and location, the brethren, and the circumstances of his prayer are not specified.

narration.text: I do not glory of myself
then is my soul filled with joy

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The phrase “instrument in the hands of God” is figurative.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal hand, an unprovided prayer scene, or the brethren as a specific named group.

title: Remembering deliverance
summary: The speaker remembers his fathers' captivity and says the Lord delivered them from bondage and established his church. He also recalls deliverance from the hands of the Egyptians.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker remembers the captivity of his fathers.
The speaker says the Lord delivered them from bondage and thereby established his church.
The speaker says the same God delivered them from the hands of the Egyptians and from bondage.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The recollections can be conveyed through off-screen narration rather than staged as present action.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker's appearance and surroundings are not described.
The fathers, Egyptians, and circumstances of the past deliverances are not visually described.

narration.text: for I surely do know that the Lord did deliver them out of bondage, and by this did establish his church;
Yea, I have always remembered the captivity of my fathers; and that same God who delivered them out of the hands of the Egyptians did deliver them out of bondage.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The deliverances are recalled, not narrated as events occurring in the scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the captivity or deliverances as present action.
Do not invent appearances, locations, or circumstances for the people mentioned.

title: Called to preach
summary: The speaker says God established his church among his fathers, called him to preach to this people, and gave him success; he also rejoices in his brethren's success in the land of Nephi.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says God established his church among his fathers and called him to preach to this people, giving him success.
He says his joy is fuller because of his brethren's success after going to the land of Nephi.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Off-screen narration may continue over an unspecified setting; the brethren's earlier journey is reported, not shown as occurring now.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker, his audience, his brethren, and the setting are not described.

narration.text: hath called me by a holy calling
the success of my brethren, who have been up to the land of Nephi.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The land of Nephi is mentioned as the location of the brethren's reported work, not the current setting.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray the brethren traveling or preaching as a present event.

title: Fruit of their labor
summary: The speaker says his brethren labored exceedingly and brought forth much fruit; remembering their success fills him with such joy that he describes his soul as carried away from the body, as it were.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says his brethren labored exceedingly and brought forth much fruit, and wonders at their reward.
He describes his soul as carried away from the body, as it were, because of the greatness of his joy at their success.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Keep the brethren's labor in off-screen recollection; the soul's separation is explicitly qualified as figurative.
unspecified_visual_details: The brethren's identities, appearance, work locations, and any literal bodily or spiritual visual details are unspecified.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: “Much fruit” and the soul being carried away are figures of speech in this passage.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict literal fruit, a separated soul, or the brethren's labor as a present scene.

title: A closing prayer
summary: The speaker prays that his brethren and those who are the fruit of their labors may enter and remain in God's kingdom and praise him forever; he closes with Amen.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker asks God to grant that his brethren may sit in God's kingdom and that those who are the fruit of their labors may go no more out and praise God forever.
The speaker asks that it be done according to his words and ends with Amen.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Present the prayer as off-screen narration over an unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker, brethren, those who benefited from their labors, and the kingdom's appearance are not specified.

narration.text: may God grant unto these, my brethren

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a prayer and wish, not a narrated vision of the kingdom.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the kingdom or its inhabitants as a visible event.
